review_notes: I read the whole file and concentrated on repeated proof blocks. I looked for the same reasoning in the NoethBC20 and NoethKit19 comparison lemmas, in the three finite-type/FG blocks, and in the EndKit19 and SpreadKit19 sections. I checked Mathlib's FiniteType and Finiteness files for a ready-made FG transitivity lemma and found none (`Algebra.FiniteType.trans` is only the underlying step). Nothing was compiled, so the rewrites are sketches. In finding 1, the `hmul` hypotheses match up to proof-irrelevant subtype proofs, and the identification of the two comparison maps follows from `pullback.hom_ext` with the `hg_fst`/`hg_snd` facts. Smaller repeats I judged too short or too local to report: `hP` in `fst_comp_fst_comp_eq_of_rel` and `fst_comp_mulMor_comp_eq_of_rel`, the `h1`/`h2` branches in `stage_autoHom`, the e1/e2 pairs in `lift_comp_mulMor` and `lift_comp_mulMorPush`, and the cancellation argument in `IsHom.ev_one` and `pushG_one`.

findings.problem: This is a second proof of what `NoethBC20.mul_coe_comp_bcComparison` already proves, and `isPullback_comp_transition` re-proves `NoethBC20.isPullback_bcComparison`. In both, the morphism into `pullback f ι` has first component g (resp. π) and second component p ≫ j'. The proof is the same in both: `pullback.hom_ext`, then the fst component via the hypothesis `H`/`hmul`, `baseChange_mul`, `baseChangePointOfBase_coe`, `lift_fst` and a `mul_coe_congr` lemma with the two `Subtype.ext` side goals, then the snd component via `(G.mul ..).2`. `hg_fst` and `hg_snd` re-derive the facts `bcComparison_fst` and `bcComparison_snd`. A second `mul_coe_congr` (NoethKit19, line 343) duplicates the NoethBC20 one (line 36). The file then uses the two copies in different places: `stage_endos` uses `mul_comp_transition` and `stage_autoHom` uses `NoethBC20.mul_coe_comp_bcComparison`.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma identifying the two morphisms. For `r` with `hr_fst`/`hr_snd` it would read `hπ.isoPullback.hom ≫ r = NoethBC20.bcComparison (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R₁ ↥T))) p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R₁ L))) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom T.val.toRingHom)) (specMap_val_comp T) π hπ`. The proof is `pullback.hom_ext` using the existing `hg_fst` and `hg_snd` computations (via `hπ.isoPullback_hom_fst`/`_snd`, `hr_fst`, `hr_snd`) against `bcComparison_fst`/`_snd`. Then `isPullback_comp_transition` becomes `this ▸ NoethBC20.isPullback_bcComparison ..`. `mul_comp_transition` becomes `rw [this]; exact NoethBC20.mul_coe_comp_bcComparison .. hmul t' x y`. The `R'`, `ι`, `j`, `j'`, `hj` arguments are instantiated with T, `algebraMap R₁ ↥T`, `algebraMap R₁ L`, `T.val` and `specMap_val_comp T`. Delete the NoethKit19 `mul_coe_congr` and the duplicated `hg_fst`/`hg_snd`/`ht` blocks. Alternatively, build `r` in `stage_endos` from `bcComparison`-style data and drop `exists_transition`.
findings.benefit: The comparison-with-base-change multiplicativity argument, which is the substantive part, is stated and proved once. Any later change to `RelativeGroupLaw.baseChange_mul` or to the point-wise API then needs one edit instead of two. Readers no longer have to check that two near-identical 30-line proofs agree. The file also stops carrying two incompatible `mul_coe_congr` lemmas.

    (h₁ : R₁.FG) (h₂ : T.FG) : (T.restrictScalars ℤ).FG := by
findings.problem: The same four-line argument appears three times. It translates both FG hypotheses to `Algebra.FiniteType`, applies `Algebra.FiniteType.trans`, and translates back for `T.restrictScalars`. One copy is the lemma `fg_restrictScalars`, which is stated only for base ℤ. The other two are inlined as `hfg` in `stage_endos` (lines 945–949) and `stage_autoHom` (lines 1079–1083), with base `A₀` instead of ℤ. The proof does not use ℤ, so the lemma does not apply there and each caller repeats it. The lemma itself appears unused.
findings.proposed_change: Generalise the lemma to an arbitrary base: `theorem fg_restrictScalars {A₀ L : Type u} [CommRing A₀] [CommRing L] [Algebra A₀ L] (R₁ : Subalgebra A₀ L) (T : Subalgebra ↥R₁ L) (h₁ : R₁.FG) (h₂ : T.FG) : (T.restrictScalars A₀).FG`. The proof is the existing one with ℤ replaced by A₀. Then `hfg` in `stage_endos` becomes `fg_restrictScalars R₁ T hR₁fg hTfg`. In `stage_autoHom` it becomes `fg_restrictScalars T₁ T₂ hT₁fg hT₂fg`. Both `Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType` calls and the `Algebra.FiniteType.trans` step then live in one place.
findings.benefit: The two stage lemmas lose about eight lines of bookkeeping and read as the geometric argument they are. The currently dead ℤ-only lemma becomes the shared tool. The FG-transitivity fact has a single name that can be reused, for example for a chain of subalgebras.
